prompt_text: I need my roof replaced in Dallas. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but I can’t do a live web search from here, so I can’t pull an up‑to‑the‑minute list of Dallas roofers. I can either (A) show you how to find the best, verified local companies and give a ready-to-use vetting checklist and phone/email script, or (B) if you paste a few company names you’ve found, I’ll evaluate them and tell you which to call first and why.

Which do you want? If you want me to proceed without providing names, here’s a concise, practical plan you can use right away to find and pick the right Dallas roofer.

Quick plan to find specific Dallas roofing companies to call
1) Where to search (fast, reputable sources)
- GAF Contractor Locator and Owens Corning Contractor Locator — these list Master Elite / Platinum contractors who meet training and warranty standards.  
- BBB (Better Business Bureau) — check rating and complaints.  
- Google Business / Google Maps — look for 4.5+ stars with recent, local reviews.  
- Nextdoor and local Facebook groups — for real neighborhood referrals (very useful in Dallas neighborhoods).  
- Angi (formerly Angie’s List), HomeAdvisor — good for project history and customer reviews.  
- Local insurance restoration lists — if you’re covering an insurance claim, ask your adjuster which contractors they recommend (but beware conflicts of interest).

2) Which types of companies to contact (call 3–5)
- A GAF Master Elite or Owens Corning Platinum/Preferred local contractor (for certified installation and extended manufacturer warranties).  
- A long-established Dallas family-owned roofer with many local references (they know Dallas hail/wind patterns and permitting).  
- A storm‑damage/insurance restoration specialist if you suspect hail or storm damage.  
- A reputable national company with local crews (for capacity and standardized processes).  
- One lower-cost local contractor for comparison only — but vet carefully.

3) What to ask on the phone / in your first email (short script)
- “Are you licensed/registered to do roofing in the City of Dallas? Can you provide your registration number?”  
- “Are you a GAF/Owens Corning/CertainTeed certified installer? Which manufacturer warranties do you offer?”  
- “Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Can I see certificates?”  
- “Can you provide three local references (last 12–24 months) with similar roofs?”  
- “Will you pull required Dallas permits and handle inspections?”  
- “Do you do a full tear‑off or roof-over? What materials and underlayment do you use?”  
- “What is your payment schedule and start-to-finish timeline?”  
- “Will you provide a written contract and manufacturer warranty in writing?”

4) How to compare bids (what must be in the written estimate)
- Detailed scope (tear-off count, # of layers, decking repair included or priced separately).  
- Exact materials: shingle brand/model, underlayment, ice/water shield, flashing, nails (type and count), venting changes.  
- Permit and disposal fees included? Dumpster or haul-off specified.  
- Start date and estimated completion date.  
- Payment schedule: avoid large upfront payments (common: 10–20% deposit, balance on completion).  
- Warranty: contractor workmanship warranty length and manufacturer warranty (and whether it’s transferable).  
- Warranty registration: will the contractor register manufacturer warranty with the maker?

5) Red flags / things to avoid
- Door-to-door storm-chasers offering “special pricing today only.”  
- No physical address or only a P.O. box.  
- Requests for full cash up-front or demands for full payment before permit/inspection.  
- Refusal to provide references, insurance certificates, or written contract.  
- Very low bid that’s significantly under others — often cuts corners.

6) Dallas-specific considerations
- Hail and wind are common — make sure shingles have adequate impact and wind ratings.  
- Dallas may require contractor registration/permits; confirm with the company and with the City of Dallas inspections office.  
- If filing an insurance claim, document everything with photos and get bids before signing assignment-of-benefits agreements.

7) If you want, I can prepare:
- A tailored 3–5 question phone script for a specific contractor type.  
- A one-page comparison checklist you can print and bring to appointments.  
- A sample contract addendum to protect you (payment schedule, permit confirmation, lien waiver).

Next step — tell me:
- Your Dallas ZIP or neighborhood, roof size/age (approx.), material you want (asphalt shingle, metal, tile), and whether this will involve an insurance claim.  
If you give me a ZIP / neighborhood I can guide you exactly how to run quick searches (including search terms) and which local certifiers to prioritize — or you can paste a few company names you’ve found and I’ll evaluate them for you. Which do you prefer?
